writeup: TIC 313498432 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 54.888249 days and a primary eclipse depth of 0.10% dimming. The automated transit-search pipeline identified this target with a detection significance of 38.7 and a machine-learning confidence score of 0.96. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal at a peak signal-to-noise of 9.6, though the centroid offset of 17.5 arcsec warrants attention. No secondary eclipse was detected. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, an automated data-quality check found that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth - a pattern suggesting the true orbital period may be twice the initially measured value. While pixel-confirmation and eclipse timing remain unaffected by this finding, the alternating-depth signature represents an open question about the system's true nature.
